subsystems.name: Battery pack
subsystems.role: stores electrical energy in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, chosen for safety and long cycle life.

subsystems.name: Battery management system
subsystems.role: keeps every cell within safe voltage and temperature limits and balances charge between them.

subsystems.name: Hybrid inverter
subsystems.role: converts DC battery power to grid-quality AC and back, and manages power flow from solar, battery, grid and backup loads.

subsystems.name: Energy management controller
subsystems.role: decides moment to moment whether to charge, discharge, or pass grid power through, based on tariffs, solar output and backup needs.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: keeps the cells and power electronics within their operating temperature range.

subsystems.name: Backup power interface
subsystems.role: isolates the home from the grid during an outage and supplies dedicated critical loads.

subsystems.name: Enclosure and mounting
subsystems.role: houses the system indoors or outdoors and fixes it to a wall or floor.

buildSteps.title: Make the cells
buildSteps.detail: LFP cathode and graphite anode materials are coated onto metal foil, wound or stacked with a separator and electrolyte, then sealed into cells and formed through initial charge cycles.

buildSteps.title: Assemble modules and packs
buildSteps.detail: Cells are grouped into modules, connected with busbars, and stacked into a pack with compression frames and electrical insulation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the battery management system
buildSteps.detail: Voltage and temperature sensors are attached to each cell group, and the BMS board is wired to control contactors, fuses and balancing circuits.

buildSteps.title: Build the hybrid inverter
buildSteps.detail: Power semiconductor switches, inductors, capacitors and control boards are assembled onto heatsinks, then firmware is loaded to manage grid synchronisation and islanding.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the complete unit
buildSteps.detail: The battery pack, inverter, thermal system and controls are fitted into the enclosure and connected with internal power and data cables.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: Each unit runs through charge and discharge cycles, grid-interaction tests, and safety checks for insulation, grounding and thermal performance before certification.

buildSteps.title: Install in the home
buildSteps.detail: The unit is mounted on a wall or floor, wired to the main electrical panel and a critical loads sub-panel, and connected to solar or grid inputs as required.

buildSteps.title: Commission and connect
buildSteps.detail: The installer configures backup circuits, tariff schedules and grid settings, then verifies that the system switches to backup during a simulated outage.

prerequisites.why: LFP chemistry offers a good balance of safety, cycle life and cost for stationary storage.
they convert between battery DC and grid AC, and manage multiple power sources seamlessly.
rules for anti-islanding, voltage and frequency ride-through let batteries safely share the grid.
a suitable panel, wiring and a critical loads sub-panel are needed to isolate and power essential circuits.

pathway.milestone: single-home batteries for blackout backup and solar self-consumption
pathway.unlocks: resilience for individual households and better use of rooftop solar.

pathway.milestone: home batteries aggregated into virtual power plants
pathway.unlocks: grid services such as peak shaving and frequency response from many small batteries.

pathway.milestone: integration with electric vehicles for vehicle-to-home backup
pathway.unlocks: much larger backup capacity without buying a separate stationary battery.

pathway.milestone: widespread adoption with longer-duration and lower-cost systems
pathway.unlocks: a more flexible, decentralised grid that can absorb more renewable generation.
